runs.answer:

- Stores raise prices when things cost them more to make, or when lots of people want to buy the same things.

runs.answer: Inflation means things cost more money over time. Imagine a candy bar that cost $1 last year but costs $1.10 now. Your money buys less candy than it used to. That's inflation! Prices keep creeping up, so the same dollar can't buy as much as it could before.

Imagine you buy a candy bar for one dollar. Next year, the same candy bar costs two dollars. Your dollar can't buy as much as it used to. That's inflation: when prices go up over time, your money buys less.

ablations.prompt: Help me explain inflation to a 10-year-old. Give me exactly 3 bullet points, and use simple words a fifth grader would understand.

runs.answer:
- Inflation means prices go up over time. A candy bar that cost 50 cents when your parents were kids might cost a dollar today.

- Money buys less when inflation happens. With the same $5, you can buy fewer things than you could last year.

- Grown-ups watch inflation closely. When prices rise too fast, banks and the government try to slow it down so prices don't get out of control.

- Inflation means prices go up over time, so the same amount of money buys fewer things. A candy bar that cost 50 cents might cost a dollar later.
- Lots of things can make prices go up, like when people want to buy more stuff than businesses can make, or when it costs more to make things.
- Money loses a little bit of its power when prices rise, so your savings can buy less than before unless they grow too.
